PHP opening tag; scope supplied in question metadata

results.contract: OWASP destination and redirect contract; no live DNS, SSRF probing or complete production filter is claimed.

optionReview.rationale: An allowed initial endpoint can redirect to a destination outside the permitted boundary.
TLS authenticates a connection’s peer; it does not prove that destination is allowed for this feature.
Alternate addresses, DNS resolution and redirects can still reach forbidden destinations.
URL syntax alone does not establish an allowed destination. Use validated business input, an explicit destination policy, connection-time network controls and redirects that cannot escape the policy.

results.contract: OWASP storage/delivery boundary applied to an explicit download-only requirement. No uploaded active document is executed.

optionReview.rationale: HttpOnly limits cookie reads but does not prevent active content from acting within that origin.
A different filename does not remove the active-content origin risk.
Identifying it as HTML does not make its script content trusted.

An isolated delivery origin and attachment disposition avoid treating uploaded HTML as an inline page of the authenticated application; upload authorization and validation remain separate requirements.

results.contract: MDN browser cookie contract. This does not claim a live browser attack simulation.

optionReview.rationale: HttpOnly does not distinguish those methods or stop automatic cookie attachment.
HttpOnly prevents reading the cookie value but does not block fetch from sending eligible cookies.
Eligible form submissions also carry cookies; script access to the value is not required.
Preventing direct access to the cookie value does not prevent the browser from attaching it to a request.

results.contract: Laravel official Nginx deployment example restricts FastCGI to the front controller and returns 404 for other PHP locations. No live Nginx instance is tested.

optionReview.rationale: The document root is correct but this still permits additional PHP files to execute.
That prevents Laravel from executing and may disclose source rather than safely rejecting PHP paths.
A narrow FastCGI entry point plus rejection of other PHP paths enforces the stated execution boundary.
A separate PHP script can execute without entering Laravel’s front controller or middleware.

results.contract: Official deployment permission contract; no host ownership or permissions are modified.

optionReview.rationale: That permits the writes but unnecessarily lets the runtime account modify executable application source.
Warming views does not eliminate ongoing log and file-session writes.
Laravel uses those runtime/cache directories while normal application source need not be writable by the worker.
Public asset access does not supply the configured log, session and compiled-view write paths.

results.contract: Migration reversal is an explicit operation. The release-switch decision additionally follows the stated shared-state and data-retention constraints; no production rollback is executed.

optionReview.rationale: Switching code artifacts does not revert the database; compatibility must be checked without assuming new writes can be discarded.
That can destroy new data or reverse compatible additions unnecessarily; recovery must first assess current-state compatibility.
That can discard the user writes the scenario explicitly requires retaining.
A retained code directory is not a snapshot of the shared database.

results.contract: The real production-confirmation branch explicitly accepts --force. No real deployment command is run.

optionReview.rationale: Pretend displays intended SQL rather than applying the migrations.
Suppressing interaction alone is not affirmative consent to the production confirmation.
The force option tells the production confirmation guard to proceed; it does not make the migrations reversible or transactionally safe.
Status reports migration state rather than running pending migrations.

results.contract: Official Octane worker-reload contract. Octane server software is not installed or exercised in this isolated harness.

optionReview.rationale: Regenerating autoload metadata does not unload classes already present in a long-lived PHP process.
That targets queue workers rather than the persistent HTTP workers described.
Octane’s reload command restarts its application workers so they load the changed code.
View cache invalidation does not generally replace already loaded application classes.

results.contract: PostgreSQL index overhead contract plus the stated workload. No PostgreSQL benchmark or production index is executed.

optionReview.rationale: Schema operability matters but does not measure production read/write tradeoffs.
That confirms an isolated read improvement but does not assess the stated frequent-write workload.
An index can improve a read while imposing maintenance and storage costs elsewhere; the full workload determines the tradeoff.
That is useful capacity evidence but does not cover the frequent-write maintenance cost and overall workload tradeoff.

results.contract: Documented idempotency/failure ambiguity plus the explicit provider contract. No real payment, network request or production recovery is executed.

optionReview.rationale: The provider might not have committed it; a timeout also does not prove success.
The outcome is unknown; retaining the operation identity lets recovery discover or replay the original result without intentionally creating a new charge.
A new key can create a second charge when the first already succeeded.
A local database rollback cannot undo an independently committed provider operation.

results.contract: Composer lock/install contract and the Laravel upgrade guide. This is a validation-planning question, not a claim to have upgraded an unrelated production application.

optionReview.rationale: Dependency resolution establishes installable constraints; it does not prove application behavior across changed framework contracts.
Unchanged caller code may still observe changed dependency behavior.
Reproducing dependency installation is useful but still does not exercise application behavior.
Syntax validity cannot detect behavioral changes in routing, validation or persistence.
